summary: Persistent 429s during nightly bulk ingest coinciding with health probes and staggered refill windows
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports recurring 429 responses during nightly bulk embedding job (concurrent with a separate real-time ingestion stream). Errors began after a recent upgrade to the dedicated pool autoscaler and after enabling a new health-check probe on edge proxies.

Impact: Large nightly backfill jobs are failing mid-run with sustained 429s, causing customer SLA misses for their downstream indexing pipeline. A subset of live realtime requests also observe short-lived 429 spikes.

Environment: Dedicated pool in eu-west, production. Customer uses ephemeral short-lived keys for parallel workers and a long-lived key for realtime traffic.

Key observation: Throttles appear aligned with health-check heartbeat windows and bulk job worker warmup. Token-refill windows between the edge proxies and central rate-limiter appear misaligned, resulting in brief double-accounting of requests during the refill boundary.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a dedicated pool in eu-west with default burst window (60s) and token refill of X tokens/second.
2) Start a bulk embed backfill with 300 parallel workers using ephemeral keys and small payloads (avg 120ms per request).
3) Start a separate realtime low-volume stream concurrently (long-lived key).
4) Enable a 10s health-check probe on edge proxies that issues lightweight GETs to the ingest endpoint every 10s.
5) Observe client-side 429s in the bulk workers after ~5-10 minutes concentrated around proxy health-check heartbeat boundaries.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:15:11Z token-refill-sync scheduled at 2026-03-10T02:15:10.900Z delta=+2 tokens (edge), central-refill=0
client-error worker-237 failed request id=abc123 status=429 body=\"quota_exceeded\" retry-after=25
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Health-check heartbeats briefly increment per-connection accounting on the edge which offsets the token bucket boundary, causing a transient double-accounting at central rate limiter.
Hypothesis 2: Ephemeral worker keys created en masse are hitting a per-key concurrency window which, combined with per-tenant token smoothing, exhausts the tenant bucket at refill boundary.
Evidence: 429s cluster with timestamps immediately after health-checks and at central refill boundaries (see logs). Edge proxies show an extra +1 token delta at those windows.
SRE ran a query across rate-limiter metrics: spike in "throttle.count" aligned with edge HCs and with peak ephemeral-key creation events from the bulk job.
Initial mitigation tested: disabling health-check on a staging route removed tight 429 clusters in a controlled replay, suggesting probe interaction contributes materially.
Next steps: need to coordinate with infra to evaluate token-refill alignment logic and consider adding per-route quota separation for bulk ingest vs realtime paths for this customer.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Priya Rao (Support): Thanks for the report, @Alexei. We've replicated a concentrated 429 cluster in a replay environment when we enabled a 10s probe. Can you provide the exact worker startup pattern (concurrency ramp and key TTL)?
2026-03-10 09:47 - Alexei Petrov (LumenDocs): Worker ramp: we spawn 300 workers over 30s then steady. Ephemeral keys are 5 minute TTL. Bulk throughput target ~1200 req/s. Realtime stream ~30 req/s.

2026-03-10 12:03 - Danilo Martins (SRE): We see edge token delta events at the same second as the refill boundary. We're going to instrument the refill handshake and add a tagging field to trace which refill source applied tokens (edge vs central).

2026-03-11 07:21 - Rafael Ortiz (Assigned): Short-term workaround proposed: 1) Increase burst window to 120s for the dedicated pool, 2) Segregate bulk ingest route with a separate quota, 3) Advise customer to stagger worker ramp by 2s. Rafael will schedule a config change for a limited window to validate.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Alexei Petrov (LumenDocs): Will test staggered ramping tonight and report. Appreciate the temporary burst increase. Any risk to realtime SLA when increasing burst window?
resolution: Workaround applied: increased dedicated pool burst window to 120s for LumenDocs and created a separate per-route quota for /v1/embeddings-bulk to isolate backfills from realtime traffic. Customer agreed to stagger worker ramp (2s jitter). SRE to deploy a patch to tag refill-origin in rate-limiter logs and schedule a follow-up to evaluate permanent fix (align refill handshake between edge and central). Follow-up action: infra ticket to change refill boundary algorithm and add per-tenant window smoothing (task INT-30342).
follow_up_actions: Create infra bug to investigate refill handshake and race conditions (INT-30342).
Add metric: refill_origin tagged in throttle logs and dashboard (SLO impact check).
Draft best-practice doc for customers on worker ramp jitter and ephemeral key TTLs for bulk ingestion (owner: Developer Experience).
